title: SanitizeControlChars must strip full unicode control range, not just ASCII
answers: Why are C1 control characters (0x80-0x9F) not stripped from plugin origin or header values?
How should I sanitize untrusted strings used in metric labels or HTTP headers?
SanitizeControlChars isn't removing all control characters
body:
Symptom: untrusted strings (plugin IDs used as metric label values, datasource header values during alert eval) could still contain non-ASCII control characters like U+0085/U+009F after sanitization.
Root cause: pkg/util/strings.go:SanitizeControlChars only filtered runes with r < 0x20 or r == 0x7f, missing the Unicode C1 control range (0x80-0x9F).
Fix pattern: use unicode.IsControl(r) instead of hand-rolled ASCII range checks when stripping control characters from untrusted input that feeds metric labels, headers, or log/trace attributes.
Constraints: applies whenever sanitizing strings for use as metric label values or outgoing header values; TruncateUTF8 byte-truncation afterward is unaffected and still required to cap size.
applies: pkg/util/strings.go SanitizeControlChars and its callers (plugin origin metric label, eval datasource header sanitization)

search: SanitizeControlChars implementation must use unicode.IsControl(r) instead of ASCII range checks to catch full Unicode control range including C1 controls (0x80-0x9F), not just ASCII (r < 0x20 or r == 0x7f). Required for untrusted strings used as metric label values or outgoing header values in ngalert datasource eval and plugin origin metrics. TruncateUTF8 byte-length capping must still follow sanitization. Located in pkg/util/strings.go:SanitizeControlChars and consulted by pkg/services/ngalert/schedule/metrics.go and eval datasource header paths.
